note:
Completed-season records, used as the prior a small in-season sample gets shrunk toward.

This exists because of a specific failure: after one gameweek of 2026/27 the model dropped Haaland, who had taken five shots against Bournemouth without scoring. No human would do that, because a human knows he scored 27 league goals last season and 22 the season before. The model had no way to know that. Now it does.

Seeded by hand from published season reviews, and only where the figure was clearly and consistently reported -- `scripts/fetch_history.py` replaces this wholesale with the official `history_past` numbers straight from the FPL API, which is exact and free. Until that has run, a player absent from this file has no prior, which the model treats as 'unknown', never as 'bad'. A newly promoted striker with no Premier League record must not be scored as though he had a bad one.

`minutes` is omitted where the published source didn't carry it. Per-90 rates are then unavailable and read as zero; points-per-appearance, which is what actually feeds the projection, works from totals alone.
sources: premierleague.com — FPL records and stats from 2024/25; FPL 2025/26 Team of the Season
theanalyst.com (Opta) — Haaland or no Haaland? The If, When and Why for FPL Managers
